---
id: F06-directive-shape
tests: the directive is one imperative act with a date, a binary test, and a prediction
threshold: 1.0
---

## Session

**Founder:** We sell inventory software to independent hardware stores. 14
customers at $400 a month, and I'm the only one working on it, no outside money,
covering my costs since March. Six cancelled in the last two months so I called
all six of them last week. Four said the same thing, that their staff kept
entering counts wrong and they stopped trusting the numbers. The other two said
it was too expensive. I want to work out what to build so the next six don't
leave.

## Must

- End with exactly one directive
- State the directive as an observable act the founder performs, not something to think about, explore, research, or consider
- Include a specific date
- Include a verification test a third party could check as either true or false
- Include a prediction of what the founder will find

## Must not

- Offer more than one thing to do
- Use hedging language such as "you might want to", "consider", "one option would be", or "I'd recommend exploring"
- Hand back a document, plan, or written summary as the action itself
- Give the founder a task that plainly takes longer than seven days

## Notes

This fixture tests directive shape only, so the session is deliberately clean of
anything on the outranking ladder. Solo, so no team fracture. Covering costs and
no raise mentioned, so no cash signal. The churned customers have already been
called, so no demand-contact signal. Shipped and selling, so nothing on building
without shipping.

An earlier version had the founder say "I haven't asked any of them," which is a
rung 3 signal. That made the interrupt a legitimate response, and an interrupt
ends its turn at the consent beat with no directive in it, so correct behavior
failed the test one run in three. If you edit this session, keep it free of
ladder signals or you are testing the interrupt instead of the directive.
